paper.title: Predicting zinc binding at the proteome level
paper.citation: Passerini A, Andreini C, Menchetti S, Rosato A, Frasconi P. Predicting zinc binding at the proteome level. BMC Bioinformatics 8:39 (2007)

skill.name: paper2repro
skill.note: The skill text loaded in the reproduction session (2026-11-09) matches the skill folder tagged paper2repro-v0.4.0; the installed skill was at this commit.

items.label: Table 1, zinc site types

assumptions.what: Sites from today's mmCIF files of the 296 zinc chains of Additional file 1; a site is a zinc ion with at least one side-chain donor (C SG, H ND1/NE2, D OD1/OD2, E OE1/OE2, N OD1/ND2, Q OE1/NE2) of the chain within 3 A; asymmetric unit only
assumptions.sensitivity: Counting every N, O, S atom gives 452 sites but 29 ligands outside Table 2's six residue types and 3 of 11 multiple-type counts off; side-chain donors give all 11.

cause.summary: We count 450 sites in 295 chains against 464 in 305. Additional file 1 lists 296 of the 305 zinc chains, and in one of those (1H79) the metal is now modelled as iron. The deficit sits almost all in Zn4 (12 sites, 8 chains). With the donor atoms restricted to side chains of C, H, D, E, N and Q, the multiple-site-type counts of Table 1 come back exactly.

hypotheses.test: analyze_sites.py with donors=any

hypotheses.hypothesis: Only the side-chain donors of the six residue types of Table 2 count
hypotheses.test: analyze_sites.py default

hypotheses.hypothesis: The 9 chains missing from Additional file 1 carry the missing sites
hypotheses.test: deficit by site type: Zn4 -12 sites, Zn2 -2, Zn1 -1, Zn3 +1, all but Zn3 short; the chains cannot be identified

hypotheses.hypothesis: PDB entries changed since 2005
hypotheses.test: 1H79: the 4-Cys metal of the supplement's ZN_1588_A is now FE2; 1AW5 Cys219 is now beyond 3 A

items.label: Table 3, binding-site patterns

assumptions.what: A site matches a pattern when its ligands, in sequence order, have the pattern's residue types and gaps (gap = residues between, 'short' 0-7); [CHDE] x(0-7) [CHDE] x(.) [CHDE] x(0-7) [CHDE] is SLS or SSS
assumptions.sensitivity: Counting the 'x(.)' pattern as SLS only gives 135 against 161; with SSS added, 155.

cause.summary: Same sites as Table 1. 5 of 18 counts are equal; the four-ligand patterns are short by up to 12, as the Zn4 sites are.

items.label: Fig. 1a, P(X bound | Y bound) by separation

controls.name: separation as index difference (off by one)
(a) read as P(bound | a bound residue within d)

assumptions.what: Residues: the C and H of the zinc chains; separation d: the number of residues between X and Y; P(X|Y) over the pairs within d
assumptions.sensitivity: The prior is then 0.305 (published line at 0.309). Reading d as the index difference scores 62%; P(X bound | some bound residue within d) scores 19%; C, H, D and E residues score 0%.

assumptions.what: Axes from the JPEG: boxes x 46-271 and 362-587, y 49-256; log10 x from 1 to 1000; y 0.1-1 (a) and 0.1-0.6 (b)
assumptions.sensitivity: Tick labels only; nothing inside the box is fitted.

items.label: Fig. 1b, correlation of binding states by separation

controls.name: separation as index difference (off by one)

assumptions.what: As Fig. 1a: C and H residues of the zinc chains, separation = residues between, Pearson correlation over the pairs within d
assumptions.sensitivity: Index difference: 43%; x 1.05: 47%.

controls.name: Fig. 4a curves in place of these
random scores at the same share of positives

assumptions.what: PSI-BLAST (BLAST+ 2.17.0), 3 iterations, other settings default (inclusion E-value 0.002), against UniRef100 release 2010_01 (9,808,438 sequences): the 2005 NCBI nr is not archived and the paper gives no settings
assumptions.sensitivity: Not varied (a second database means another 60 CPU hours of PSI-BLAST). The tuned SVM and Platt parameters of Additional file 1 were kept although they were fitted on 2005 profiles.

assumptions.what: Descriptor: the 20 weighted observed percentages divided by 100, information per position in bits and relative weight as printed by PSI-BLAST, a flag that is 1 outside the chain; no other scaling
assumptions.sensitivity: With percentages left at 0-100 the Gaussian width 0.1 of Additional file 1 would make every kernel value zero; this scale is the one that fits the published widths.

assumptions.what: scikit-learn 1.9.1 SVC (LIBSVM) with an RBF kernel on explicit feature maps; one C for both classes; Platt constants of Additional file 1, not refitted
assumptions.sensitivity: The semi-pattern kernel of Eq. 1 is the dot product of the feature map exactly (package test). Class weights are not stated in the paper.

assumptions.what: Supplement positions mapped to today's SEQRES; 15 chains need an offset (remediation added or removed leading residues); 28 of 13,837 LOO residues (16 whose letter differs and 12 of two chains that no longer exist) are left out
assumptions.sensitivity: 0.2% of the residues.

cause.summary: The profiles are not the paper's: the 2005 nr is gone, so ours come from UniRef100 of 2010 with unstated PSI-BLAST settings, and the SVM and Platt parameters tuned on the old profiles were kept. The labels, folds and residues are the paper's own.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The printed AURPC is the area under the drawn curve
hypotheses.test: Area under the published curves (read from the PDF): LOO 0.624 and 0.666, CV 0.462 and 0.531, all 0.031-0.034 above the printed 0.590, 0.633, 0.428, 0.500; on our curves the drawn area and average precision differ by 0.002 or less on the C and H panels (at most 0.007 on any panel)

hypotheses.hypothesis: The printed AURPC averages the five CV folds
hypotheses.test: Fold-averaged average precision of our CV: 0.493 and 0.551, pooled 0.494 and 0.552

hypotheses.hypothesis: Residues lost in the mapping to today's SEQRES
hypotheses.test: 28 of 13,837 LOO residues (0.2%) dropped
